column2: Definition: Creative narration of real or imaginary events using imagination

column3: Based on a Picture: Develop a story using elements or theme from a visual prompt
Based on an Outline: Expand given points or sequence into a complete story
Completing a Story: Continue a story using given opening lines
Based on Clues: Build a story using hints or clues provided
Title: Catchy and relevant; should not reveal the entire plot
Structure: Introduction, plot development (middle), and conclusion
Characters: Use minimum characters; describe them vividly
Plot and Setting: Logical sequence (beginning–middle–end) with clear time and place
Twist/Climax: An interesting twist or strong climax makes the story memorable
Dialogues: Use meaningful dialogues to move the story forward

column2: Definition: Expression of personal views on a topic for newspapers or magazines

column3: Topic-Based: Based on a given subject or issue
Visual-Based: Based on interpretation of images, charts, or pictures
Format

column4: Body: Main content of the article

column3: Body Structure

column4: Introduction: Define topic or begin with an engaging opening
Analysis: Causes, effects, problems, and solutions
Conclusion: Summary with a strong closing statement

column3: Language: Balanced formal–informal tone with linking words
Arguments: Support ideas with facts and examples

column2: Definition: Writing that creates a mental picture of a person, place, or event

column3: Person: Physical appearance, profession, and qualities
Place: Location, history, weather, and attractions
Event: Description of a specific occasion or experience
Show, Don’t Tell: Describe actions and scenes instead of plain facts
Sensory Details: Use sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch
Figurative Language: Use similes and analogies for creativity
Logical Order: Present ideas in a clear, organized sequence
Tense: Past tense is mandatory for past events

column2: Definition: Personal and informal record of thoughts and feelings

column3: Format: Day, Date, Time (top left), followed by “Dear Diary”
Perspective: Always first person (I, me, my)
Tone: Friendly, informal, and conversational
Content: Focus on important events and emotions
Honesty: Express true feelings and reactions
Organization: Follow chronological order
Conclusion: End with name/signature; avoid very long sentencesFormal Letter

column2: Definition: Professional correspondence written to officials or organizations

column3: Sender’s Address: Your address and contact details
Date: Standard format (e.g., 9 December 2022)
Receiver’s Designation and Address: Position and organization address
Subject: One-line summary of purpose (5–6 words)
Salutation: Sir/Madam or Respected Sir/Madam
Body Paragraphs

column4: Para 1: Introduction and reason for writing
Para 2: Detailed explanation of the issue or matter
Para 3: Expected action or response from the recipient

column3: Complimentary Close: Yours faithfully / Yours sincerely + name
Editorial Letter: Written to the editor highlighting social/public issues

column4: Key Point: Use opening “Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper…”

column3: Letter of Inquiry: Used to seek information about a course, product, or service

column4: Key Point: Mention source of information and deadline

column3: Letter of Placing Order: Used to purchase goods in bulk

column4: Key Point: List items in a table (serial no., item name, quantity); mention payment and discounts

column3: Letter of Order Cancellation: Used to cancel a previously placed order

column4: Key Point: Always mention original order number and date

column3: Letter of Complaint: Used to report defects or civic problems

column4: Key Point: Be polite but firm; describe the issue clearly
